answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing jobs that counterparties verify and by leaving a stake that is slashed when a claim is proven false. A new identity starts with no verified history, so splitting one operator across jade, willow, and umber accounts does not multiply trust; each must independently win work, lock capital, and risk losing it. Sybils therefore cost the attacker time and scarce funds, while colluding accounts cannot cheaply manufacture independent endorsements.
